items.title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
items.abstract_or_text: Background and Objective: Early and reliable disease prediction from structured clinical data remains challenging when datasets are small, highly imbalanced, and contain limited positive disease cases. Conventional machine learning (ML) and deep learning approaches often struggle to capture clinically meaningful relationships under such low-data representation conditions due to weak statistical associations between features and prediction targets. This study proposes a clinically grounded GPT2-based table-to-text framework for disease prediction using structured healthcare datasets, motivated by the contextual reasoning capability of GPT models to better capture clinically meaningful relationships when statistical learning alone becomes insufficient due to limited data availability. Methods & Materials: Structured clinical records were transformed into physician-style textual descriptions and enriched through GPT4-generated medical paraphrasing to improve minority-class representation while preserving clinical meaning. Both the original and generated clinical texts were used to fine-tune a GPT2 model across four public healthcare datasets, including heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence. Gradient-based explainable AI analysis was additionally incorporated to identify clinically important features influencing prediction outcomes. Results: The proposed framework demonstrated consistently strong predictive performance with average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively. The model achieved improved sensitivity, stronger generalization, and more stable predictive behavior compared with traditional ML, deep learning, transformer-based, and GAN-augmented approaches. Importantly, the framework consistently emphasized clinically meaningful variables even under severe class imbalance where conventional ML and neural network models often struggled. Conclusions: The proposed GPT2-based table-to-text framework provides a practical and clinically interpretable approach for disease prediction from limited structured healthcare data. By integrating contextual clinical reasoning with explainable prediction mechanisms, the framework demonstrates strong potential for early risk detection, transparent clinical decision support, and reliable deployment in real-world low-resource healthcare environments.

items.title: Application of Bayesian-Derived Gene Interaction Network and Subnetwork for Classification of Idiopathic Parkinson Disease with Biomarkers
items.abstract_or_text: Given the expenses associated with Parkinson Disease (PD), it is imperative to develop a method for accurate diagnosis before emergence of motor symptoms. While there are tests that can measure early onset of PD, these tests still rely on subjective input from patients and can thus be biased. Factors influencing their accuracy include environmental agents such as education and culture. Thus, blood-based transcriptomic signatures are a promising direction for biomarkers in PD that are minimally invasive and more objective than clinical evaluation. In this paper, we analyzed gene expression from the PPMI cohort. Using a Bayesian framework, a gene interaction network was constructed to enhance differential expressed genes (DEG) analysis through signal diffusion. In tandem with clinical traits, 13 genes were selected for optimal discrimination using a random forest model. Within the holdout test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.972, outperforming contemporary models. The model performance demonstrates the potential of using blood-based transcriptomics to enhance clinical diagnosis of PD. Other genes recovered by network diffusion but missed by traditional DEG analysis are already validated as potential biomarkers in contemporary PD research. By combining transcriptomic signatures with clinical evaluation, accurate diagnosis of PD can happen before the major destruction of dopaminergic neurons, which is critical for effective intervention and treatment.

items.title: Enhancing molecular and genomic approaches for Bordetella pertussis investigation and public health surveillance in Victoria, Australia
items.abstract_or_text: Bordetella pertussis is the main aetiological agent of pertussis (whooping cough), with a global resurgence of cases reported in 2024. As current pertussis diagnostics are predominantly based on molecular methods, cultured isolates are increasingly scarce, limiting traditional culture-based surveillance. To address these challenges, this study evaluated culture-independent approaches for B. pertussis surveillance and their feasibility for implementation in public health laboratory settings in Victoria, Australia. The Microbiological Diagnostic Unit Public Health Laboratory received 356 nasopharyngeal clinical specimens that were PCR-positive for Bordetella spp. from diagnostic laboratories for further characterisation during the 2024-2025 epidemic period. Culture-based approaches yielded only five B. pertussis isolates, largely due to limitations associated with specimen transport media. Four culture-independent approaches were evaluated for B. pertussis characterisation: real-time PCR assay for high-resolution Bordetella spp. differentiation (n=356), multiplex PCR amplicon sequencing assay for lineage typing (n=38), in-house laboratory developed test implemented on Panther Fusion(R) System for macrolide resistance screening (n=92) and shotgun metagenomic sequencing (n=5). The dataset was dominated by B. pertussis (330/356; 92.7%) with most strains harbouring ptxP3 (35/38; 92.1%) allele and the macrolide resistance rate was reported as 4.3% (4/92). Shotgun metagenomics was able to detect B. pertussis directly from clinical samples, but the genomic recovery was limited. Evaluation of operational performance and workflow integration highlighted method-specific strengths and limitations, informing suitability for implementation in public health laboratories. This study demonstrates the potential to integrate culture-independent approaches into public health laboratory settings to strengthen B. pertussis surveillance and inform feasible workflow design amid limited culture availability.

items.title: Explainable Machine Learning-Based Diabetes Prediction Using Clinical Features: A Comparative Evaluation of Ensemble and Boosting Algorithms A Comparative Study with Explainable Artificial Intelligence Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder that requires early detection and effective management to reduce health complications. Machine learning approaches have demonstrated potential for identifying complex patterns in clinical data and improving disease prediction. This study presents a comparative analysis of multiple machine learning algorithms for diabetes prediction using clinical features. The Pima Indians Diabetes dataset containing 768 patient records and eight predictive variables was utilized in this study. Data preprocessing involved handling physiologically invalid zero values through median imputation. Five classification algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, optimized Random Forest, XGBoost, and optimized XGBoost, were developed and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC metrics. The optimized Random Forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 76.62%, while Random Forest and optimized XGBoost demonstrated superior sensitivity for identifying diabetic cases. Furthermore, SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence analysis revealed that glucose level, body mass index (BMI), and age were the most influential predictors contributing to model decisions. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning and explainable AI techniques for supporting diabetes risk prediction and clinical decision-support.

items.title: IVA, a locally deployable Intelligent Variant Analyser based on a small language model for complete case-level and trio-based genomic interpretation.
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Recent work has brought large language models (LLMs) into clinical variant interpretation. In most existing approaches, the model is confined to text-level operations, retrieving, extracting, compacting, and summarizing heterogeneous evidence, while the genuine genetic evaluation is delegated to a separate deterministic engine. Other tools employ LLMs to mine functional evidence for a single ACMG criterion, to rerank a classifier's output, or to answer isolated variant questions. Integrative genetic reasoning, by contrast, demands multi-source evidence weighing for each variant, reconciliation of inheritance with observed zygosity and parental genotypes, joint interpretation of variants in the same gene, and the derivation of a case-level conclusion. Moreover, to protect patient privacy, this must be done on hospital premises. Methods: o build an end-to-end variant interpreter that runs on local infrastructure, we benchmarked 13 small language models (SLMs) on 150 multiple-choice genetics questions and selected Qwen3.5-9B. In IVA (Intelligent Variant Analyser), a four-stage pipeline, the model assigns ACMG/AMP criteria, applies de novo, dominant, recessive, and X-linked inheritance logic to trios, and writes a structured report, while deterministic code handles retrieval, phasing, point summation, citation checking, and formatting. We evaluated IVA on synthetic scenarios, 16 solved trios, and 327 solved singleton cases of visual impairment, on a single GPU. Results: On the benchmark, Qwen3.5-9B reached a mean accuracy of 0.81, compared with 0.89 for a 1.6-trillion-parameter cloud model. In the 16 trios, IVA reported every previously identified pathogenic, likely pathogenic, or uncertain-significance variant of interest (sensitivity 100%; precision 39.5%). In the 327 singleton cases, it recovered 93% of the expert-reported causative variants and classified 82% of them as pathogenic or likely pathogenic (precision 43%). Failures fell into four recurrent classes: omission, unverified mechanism, mismatch between reasoning and label, and arithmetic errors. Conclusions: A small language model running on local hardware can serve as the reasoning layer for case-level and trio-based variant interpretation when it is surrounded by deterministic safeguards. Because its outputs are not deterministic, analyst review and prospective multicenter validation remain necessary.

items.title: Automated Variant Prioritization in Suspected Genetic Kidney Disease
items.abstract_or_text: Introduction Despite the identification of >700 genes associated with inherited kidney disease, many affected individuals presumably remain genetically undiagnosed through testing of known disease genes. Novel disease gene discovery requires interpretation of large-scale sequencing data, which remains challenging. Methods We developed the Nephro Candidate Score (N-CS), a machine learning (ML) framework for variant prioritization combining a Nephro Gene Score (N-GS), Nephro Variant Score (N-VS), and heuristic Inheritance Score. The ML-based N-GS and N-VS predict gene-disease relevance and variant pathogenicity from diverse genomic features. Clinical utility was assessed in 1452 individuals with suspected inherited kidney disease using exome-wide candidate discovery and gene-level burden analysis, with external validation using recently proposed inherited kidney disease genes. Results The N-CS showed strong predictive performance, with the XGBoost-based N-GS achieving an AUC of 0.94 and the Logistic Regression-based N-VS an AUC of 0.99 on independent test sets. A gene set enrichment analysis demonstrated significant enrichment of kidney-related biological processes among top-ranked genes (p < 0.001). In our patient cohort, N-CS-guided variant filtering recovered established disease genes and highlighted ERMP1 as a compelling candidate. Incorporating the N-GS in a polycystic kidney disease burden analysis reduced multiple-testing penalties, highlighting a moderate-effect candidate. Externally, the N-CS assigned high scores to 10 of 11 newly proposed kidney disease genes. Conclusion The N-CS is a digital framework to accelerate disease gene discovery and diagnosis. It is freely available as the NC-Scorer web tool (https://nc-scorer.kidney-genetics.org/) and a command-line interface enabling standardized, scalable candidate variant evaluation.

items.title: BioMod: Biological Module Tokenization for Single-Cell Foundation Modeling
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell foundation models typically represent cells as flat sequences of individual genes, requiring higher-order biological organization to be inferred implicitly from sparse expression profiles. Similar to the evolution from character-level to semantic tokenization in natural language processing,we hypothesize that cellular states can be more efficiently represented using biologically meaningful intermediate units. Here we present BioMod, a 50-million-parameter single-cell foundation model that introduces biological modules as representation units between genes and cells. BioMod constructs an overlapping vocabulary of 660 biological modules derived from curated pathways and data-driven gene programs, replacing thousands of gene-level inputs with compact module representations. Pretrained on approximately 73 million human cells using high-ratio module masking with an asymmetric decoder, BioMod achieves state-of-the-art performance across cell-type annotation, zero-shot batch integration, perturbation-response prediction and drug-response forecasting while maintaining a compact architecture that enables efficient inference on a single GPU. Module-level analyses further demonstrate that BioMod captures biologically meaningful cellular programs and preserves pathway-level organization.

items.title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
items.abstract_or_text: Neuroplasticity, the brain's capacity to reorganise its structure and function, is a transdiagnostic feature across psychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases and a putative mechanism of action for pharmacological interventions. [11C]-UCBJ positron emission tomography (PET), which quantifies synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) density, offers the most direct in vivo measure of human synaptic density, but its relationship to complementary, more scalable neuroimaging measures of structural and functional plasticity remains uncharacterised. We combined [11C]-UCBJ PET, diffusion weighted imaging (DWI/NODDI), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and electroencephalography (EEG)-based sensory tasks (roving mismatch negativity, MMN; visual long-term potentiation, vLTP) in 18 healthy volunteers to test the relationship between synaptic terminal SV2A density and complementary structural and functional neuroplasticity measures, and whether these relationships were reproducible following pharmacological challenge with ketamine (n = 11) or N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT; n = 7). There were no statistically significant differences in PET-derived SV2A binding potential (BPND), DWI-derived neurite orientation dispersion (ODI) and structural weighted degree (SWD), EEG-derived MMN repetition suppression, and late-phase vLTP P2 potentiation, 1 to 8 days following DMT and ketamine exposure compared to baseline. BPND was coupled with ODI across cortical regions before and after pharmacological challenge, and this relationship was tighter within visual, attentional, and frontoparietal control brain networks. SWD showed a weaker, more spatially restricted association with BPND, primarily in regions belonging to the limbic and visual brain networks, but was not replicated post-drug. No consistent association was found between BPND and functional weighted degree (FWD), derived from rs-fMRI, at baseline or after pharmacological challenge. Frontotemporal BPND was positively associated with MMN repetition suppression (r = 0.61), and occipital BPND with late-phase vLTP P2 potentiation (r = 0.54), with the MMN-BPND association replicating after pharmacological challenge (r = 0.49). These findings link synaptic terminal SV2A density in the living human brain to neurite architecture and the capacity for short-term and Hebbian-like long-term synaptic plasticity, while dissociating these relationships from generic functional connectivity and magnitude of sensory-evoked responses. These data provide cross-modal validation for DWI- and EEG-derived measures as biological indices and surrogate measures of human synaptic plasticity.

items.title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. Methods: We analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurement-process features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. Results: The held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775-0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399-0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003-0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691-0.910). Conclusions: Target-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. Because some model components and measurement-process features used information from the broader first 24 hours, the model should be interpreted as a first-24-hour treatment-association model rather than a strictly prospective pre-treatment infection predictor.

items.title: Construction and Validation of a Diagnostic Model for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Based on Pyroptosis-Related Genes
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: GERD is a common chronic digestive disorder, yet its diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of objective molecular markers are lacking. Pyroptosis may contribute to esophageal mucosal injury, but a systematic search for pyroptosis-related diagnostic genes in GERD has not been performed. In this study, we used integrated bioinformatics, machine learning, and experimental validation to identify pyroptosis-associated diagnostic biomarkers for GERD and examine their relationship with the esophageal immune microenvironment. Methods: Esophageal transcriptome data from patients with GERD were obtained from the GEO database. We intersected differentially expressed genes, WGCNA module genes, and a curated set of pyroptosis-related genes to obtain candidate genes. We constructed a diagnostic model from 113 combinations of machine learning algorithms and validated it in an independent dataset using an artificial neural network. Immune cell infiltration was estimated with CIBERSORT, and the key bioinformatics results were further checked in a rat model of GERD. Results: The machine learning pipeline identified five pyroptosis-related genes with diagnostic value: GABARAPL1, CD55, CA9, SLC4A2, and LCN2. Among these, GABARAPL1 and CD55 performed best individually, with AUCs of 0.876 and 0.862. When the two genes were fed into an artificial neural network, the AUC reached 0.919 in the training cohort and 0.900 in the test cohort. Immune profiling showed that GERD esophageal mucosa contained more resting/activated dendritic cells, M2 macrophages, and activated NK cells, but fewer CD8⁺ T cells and γδ T cells. The animal experiments confirmed that GABARAPL1 was downregulated and CD55 was upregulated in GERD tissues. Conclusion: These observations point to GABARAPL1 and CD55 as potential pyroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for GERD. They may also influence disease pathogenesis through immunomodulatory mechanisms.

items.title: Lysosomal Glycosaminoglycan Catabolism Regulates Microglial Cell State in the Developing CNS
items.abstract_or_text: Remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM), a complex structural and signaling network of the nervous system, is essential for CNS development, plasticity, and injury responses, yet how individual neural cell types contribute to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that phagocytic clearance of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major components of the ECM, is an intrinsic function of microglia in the developing CNS. Our studies reveal an unexpected finding that impaired GAG clearance shifts microglia toward a non-homeostatic cell state seen in immature and disease-associated microglia (DAM), supporting a reciprocal relationship between the ECM and microglia. Using mouse models of Mucopolysaccharidosis VII, we examined the consequences of deleting {beta}-glucuronidase (GUSB), a lysosomal enzyme required for GAG degradation. Loss of GUSB causes early accumulation of undegraded chondroitin sulfate within microglial lysosomes, as confirmed by LC-MS analysis of intracellular GAGs isolated from cortical microglia. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified Gusb-null microglia as a distinct transcriptional population enriched for a core transcriptome shared by immature and disease-associated microglia. Together, these findings establish lysosomal GAG catabolism as a pathway that links ECM remodeling to the acquisition of adult homeostatic microglial identity during CNS development.

items.title: VirtualSkin integrates skin-cell identity with intervention-response prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Human skin atlases resolve a diverse set of cellular states, yet connecting these states to their responses to intervention remains difficult across independently sampled tissues. Here we present VirtualSkin, a cell language model that aligns skin transcriptomes with biological descriptions and supports intervention conditioned response prediction. We evaluated the model across independent atlas, disease, anatomical and perturbation cohorts, with donors, studies and perturbations withheld according to the experimental design. VirtualSkin improved inflammatory skin annotation by 0.056 macro F1 points and cell text retrieval by 0.12 Recall@10 points relative to the strongest corresponding comparators. The representation retained cell identity during study integration and transferred across ageing, systemic sclerosis, lymphoma and anatomical sites. Across five intervention cohorts, response prediction improved by 0.03 0.09 response-score points, with agreement at the levels of gene expression change, gene recovery and transcriptional programs. Paired tissue trajectories provided a complementary assessment in two donors per intervention. Component ablations and pairing controls localized the predictive contributions, while uncertainty estimates supported selective prediction under distribution shift. These results connect skin-cell recognition to intervention response prediction within a common evaluation framework and define the conditions under which predictions can inform experimental prioritization.

items.title: ClinStigma: A Clinician-Guided Framework for Developing Synthetic Benchmarks of Contextual Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation
items.abstract_or_text: Objective Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate, summarize, and evaluate clinical documentation, yet standardized methods for evaluating nuanced, context-dependent clinical language remain limited. Existing approaches rely primarily on annotated clinical corpora or keyword-based methods, restricting reproducibility, public dissemination, and systematic comparison across models. We present ClinStigma, a clinician-guided framework for constructing, annotating, and evaluating synthetic benchmarks of contextual stigmatizing language, demonstrated through ClinStigma-SUD, its inaugural implementation for substance use disorder documentation. Materials and Methods Candidate clinical sentences were generated using a frontier language model and iteratively reviewed according to a clinician-developed annotation rubric refined through expert review in stigmatizing language. The resulting benchmark intentionally incorporates explicit stigmatizing, neutral, and contextually ambiguous ("gray-zone") documentation requiring clinical reasoning rather than keyword recognition. Three locally deployed open-weight LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot inference, followed by external evaluation using independently annotated clinical documentation from MIMIC-IV. Results ClinStigma-SUD consists of 500 clinician-adjudicated synthetic clinical documentation sentences. Inter-rater agreement was 98.8% across the full benchmark (Cohen's {kappa} = 0.976) and 94.0% within the intentionally ambiguous subset ({kappa} = 0.880). Under zero-shot prompting, binary accuracy ranged from 84.8% to 91.8% across evaluated models, while F1 for the ambiguous (gray) class ranged from 0.038 to 0.423. Zero-shot external evaluation on 3,716 annotated examples from the independently annotated Harrigian MIMIC-IV corpus yielded 84.4% accuracy (84.4% balanced accuracy; macro F1 0.824), against a 69.9% majority-class baseline. Stigmatizing-class F1 was 0.879 in the substance-related subgroup and 0.883 in the full external corpus. Discussion and Conclusion ClinStigma establishes a reproducible clinician-guided framework for developing synthetic evaluation benchmarks for contextual clinical language. By combining structured clinical expertise, explicit annotation guidance, synthetic benchmark generation, and external evaluation, the framework enables open, privacy-preserving evaluation of language models while providing a scalable foundation for benchmark development across additional clinical specialties, including obstetrics, emergency medicine, and mental health.

items.title: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Frontier and Local LLMs Querying a Biomedical Knowledge Graph
items.abstract_or_text: We combine GeneNetwork's 1TB structured database with its metadata as an RDF graph and an associated literature corpus. We benchmark frontier and local LLMs querying it through four architectures: document, graph and agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a combination of the three. We evaluate them on 40 domain specific expert-curated questions with a new metric: the satisfaction frequency psi (psi, i.e, the share of questions answered with precision and recall of at least 70% or an f1 of at least 60%). psi ranks systems the same way precision, recall and f1 -- a machine learning metric built from the harmonic mean of precision and recall -- but is easier to read and assess for humans. System architecture had a large effect: with full use of Claude Opus 4.8 the plain document RAG of our earlier GNQA system had a psi of 36% against 86% for our new combined tools. Delegating most of the work from Claude Opus 4.8 to a local model halved query costs while still reaching a psi of 59%.

items.title: Neural signatures of glioma progression using implanted neural interfaces
items.abstract_or_text: High-grade glioma is an incurable brain cancer with a median survival of approximately 14 months. Over the last 50 years, small improvements in patient outcomes have been overshadowed by significant progress in most other cancers. Yet, emerging research has revealed that neural circuits play an active and central role in driving glioma growth and proliferation, highlighting the nervous system as a promising avenue for both disease monitoring and therapeutic intervention. Here, we present a platform for chronically monitoring tumor progression using neural recordings in freely behaving mice with gliomas. Using this platform across multiple mouse strains and glioma models, we show that neural recordings can accurately track tumor progression in vivo. Cancer progression was consistently associated with elevated gamma-band neural activity in the tumor microenvironment across both adult glioblastoma (GBM) and pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG) cancer models. Interestingly, lower frequency neural activity exhibited distinct, cell-line specific changes over time: GBM models exhibited decreases in low frequency neural activity whereas DIPG models exhibited increases over time. Finally, using machine learning models applied to chronic neural recordings from tumor-bearing mice treated with or without standard-of-care chemotherapy (temozolomide for GBM), we accurately predicted tumor burden as inferred through in vivo bioluminescence imaging. By fitting low-dimensional mathematical models to gamma-band neural trajectories, we could further predict individual tumor growth rates over a 5-week period with high accuracy. These results establish that pathological neural-tumor interactions can be harnessed to monitor glioma progression in vivo. Coupling this monitoring capability with therapeutic electrical stimulation in the same device could open up a new class of implantable, closed-loop neurotechnologies with the potential to transform glioma treatment.

items.title: Personalised normative cardiac phenotyping reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity in cardiac shape and outcome risk
items.abstract_or_text: Standard cardiac biomarkers such as ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, and strain compress complex three-dimensional heart dynamics into a small set of predefined measurements, leaving clinically important heterogeneity unrecognised. Here we propose a personalised normative cardiac framework in which each individual is compared to a digital twin representing expected healthy cardiac function given their age, sex, and body habitus. We show that structured patterns of deviation from these normative twins, discovered through systematic exploration of a generative cardiac dynamics space, constitute novel dynamic phenotypes that are not captured by conventional biomarkers. Applied independently to two UK Biobank cardiac cohorts with distinct shape representation, a 128-dimensional four-chamber statistical shape descriptor (HeartSSM, n = 52,365) and a 64-dimensional deep generative latent space from a conditional variational mesh autoencoder (MeshHeart cVAE, n = up to 39,376), we identify reproducible, continuous deviation-from-normative-twin scores (three discrete deviation phenotypes in the HeartSSM cohort) that improve cardiovascular risk stratification beyond ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and strain. The strongest effect was seen for incident atrial fibrillation among individuals with preserved ejection fraction (at least 50%): incremental C-index delta C = +0.068 (5-fold cross-validated delta C = +0.063; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3 x 10^-8), with a separate, smaller effect for incident stroke in the same preserved-EF subgroup in the independent MeshHeart cVAE representation (which showed no signal for atrial fibrillation) (delta C = +0.024, P = 2.6 x 10^-4). Both effects were checked against placebo controls in which the deviation scores were replaced by Gaussian noise. To test whether the normative twin generalises beyond UK Biobank's specific scanning and processing pipeline, we applied the MeshHeart cVAE normative twin, unmodified, to an independent external cohort of healthy volunteers imaged at a different hospital (GenScan/Hammersmith, n = 315): deviation scores in this cohort were of comparable magnitude to the UK Biobank healthy reference (ratio of means = 1.09; Mann-Whitney P = 1.4 x 10^-5), indicating that the normative twin captures cross-site-transferable structure rather than a scanner- or pipeline-specific artefact. Our findings suggest that cardiac phenotyping can move beyond predefined measurements toward data-driven dynamic phenotypes that better capture the heterogeneity underlying cardiovascular disease risk, even among individuals whose ejection fraction appears normal.

items.title: Normative transcriptomic clues to thalamic developmental vulnerability in C9orf72-FTLD
items.abstract_or_text: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers (n=72) and non-carriers (n=48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72-associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1, a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD.

items.title: A critical evaluation of Gene Ontology priors in biologically-informed neural networks
items.abstract_or_text: Biologically-informed neural networks (BINNs) embed prior knowledge such as the Gene Ontology (GO) into their architecture to produce interpretable representations, yet whether and how this prior improves performance or interpretation remains unclear. We introduce GONNECT, a BINN incorporating GO into an autoencoder. We evaluate GO constraints in the encoder, decoder, or both on RNA-seq tumour samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), comparing against published BINNs (OntoVAE, VEGA), an unconstrained baseline, randomized priors, and untrained networks. Across various performance metrics, GO structure adds little to reconstruction or latent-space organization, frequently matched by randomized or unconstrained models. Node activations agree with a gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)-derived reference, but this agreement largely arises from the architectural constraint: it is lost when GO connections are randomized, present even before training in the encoder, and learned in the decoder. Regularized soft links outside GO (GONNECT-SL) are unstable across runs and concentrate where the ontology is sparse, compensating for the prior's constraints rather than revealing new biology. Within this setting, we find no evidence that node activations capture biological information beyond that encoded by the predefined gene sets, suggesting that their apparent interpretability largely reflects the prior imposed by the architecture.

items.title: AI-Driven Design of Next-Generation Immunoinformatics Multi-Epitope Subunit Vaccine Targeting the Most Virulent Mpox Proteome: A Structural and Kinetic Validation Framework
items.abstract_or_text: The resurgence of the Mpox virus (MPXV) highlights the urgent need for scalable, mutation-resistant countermeasures. Slow development timelines hinder traditional empirical vaccine discovery, while conventional vaccinology often yields high false-positive rates because it relies on static, linear sequence-based screening. These classical informatics filters consistently fail to predict physical structural stability or the dynamic presentation of immune cells under physiological conditions, creating a distinct translational gap between computational design and in vitro efficacy. To address these limitations, here we engineered an advanced, AI-augmented vaccine discovery pipeline targeting the most virulent components of the MPXV proteome. We systematically screened eight critical viral targets essential for replication, membrane morphogenesis, and host-cell entry to map highly conserved T-cell and B-cell epitopes. Moving beyond standard heuristic filtering, we implemented a high-fidelity deep learning validation layer: ESM-2 protein language models (pLMs) were deployed to calculate pseudo-perplexity scores across chimeric linker junctions (EAAAK, GPGPG) to guarantee structural naturalness, MHCflurry ensemble models successfully verified active intracellular antigen presentation, and structure-informed graph neural networks (GNNs) simulated the physical node-attention dynamics of the immune synapse. Finally, recurrent neural networks (RNNs)-driven mRNA kinetic modeling optimized translation initiation rates and minimum free energy profiles during in silico cloning. This multi-layered pipeline successfully yielded three structurally refined, multi-epitope vaccine constructs optimized for maximum global population coverage. ESM-2 structural validation confirmed exceptionally low perplexity scores at structural junctions, indicating that the engineered chimaeras have native-like stability and a minimized risk of proteolysis. GNN-based immune synapse modeling demonstrated highly stable binding kinetics and robust binding free energies between the target epitopes and human HLA alleles. Furthermore, RNN kinetic optimizations established that the cDNA sequences are optimized for high-yield expression in heterologous expression hosts without risk of ribosomal stalling or translational bottlenecks. This study establishes a deep learning-augmented framework that bridges the gap between theoretical sequence optimization and biopharmaceutical scalability. By validating the structural naturalness, real-world immunogenicity, and manufacturing kinetics of our vaccine chimeras, this framework presents a robust, proactive paradigm for rapid vaccine architecture against emerging orthopoxvirus threats.

items.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Machine Learning Models for Predicting Revascularization, Amputation, and Cardiovascular Mortality in At-Risk Patients
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and/or diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) are at increased risk for limb loss and death. Existing risk calculators lack consistent clinical adoption; therefore, we aimed to identify vascular and non-vascular predictors of revascularization, amputation, and cardiovascular death using data from the OMOP CDM plus vascular extension. We assembled a cohort of adults with PAD, CLTI, or DFU receiving care within the UNC Health System from 2014–2024 (n = 178,995). Using 127 vascular-specific and thousands of non-vascular HER variables, we used logistic regression with inverse probability weighting and MCMC-based dimensionality reduction to predict revascularization, amputation, and cardiovascular death. The mean age was 72.5 ± 13.9 years; 50.9% were female and 23.5% Black. The revascularization and amputation models performed well (AUC = 0.984 and 0.926, respectively), while cardiovascular mortality prediction was modest (AUC = 0.772). Revascularization predictors were dominated by arterial disease, amputation prediction was driven by treatment interactions with dementia and frailty, and cardiovascular events and risk factors were the strongest predictors of cardiovascular mortality. Prediction models derived from harmonized EHR data demonstrated strong performance for revascularization and amputation. These findings support harmonized EHR-based vascular prediction modeling and warrant multi-institutional validation.

items.title: Flavins in Focus: Vitamin B2 as a Metabolic Keystone for Neuronal Repair in Regenerating Planarians
items.abstract_or_text: Regeneration imposes substantial metabolic demands to support the reconstruction of functional tissues. Essential vitamins are indispensable metabolic cofactors, yet whether their availability is spatially organized to support local metabolic demands within regenerative tissues remains largely unknown. Here, we identify previously undescribed flavin-rich cells, referred to as 'flavinocytes', that form an extensive network that spatially organizes vitamin B2 metabolism in the planarian Schmidtea mediterranea. Using endogenous flavin autofluorescence as a label-free in vivo metabolic readout, we show that this network consists of elongated cells that form longitudinal varicosity-containing strands closely associated with the central nervous system. RNAi-mediated disruption of riboflavin uptake and metabolism reduced flavin-associated autofluorescence and its spatial distribution within the animal, while affecting blastema formation, eye regeneration, and nervous system reconstruction. These findings demonstrate that riboflavin metabolism is required for successful regeneration. Single-cell transcriptomics, protein localization, and functional perturbations further suggest a reciprocal relationship between flavinocytes and the regenerating nervous system, pointing to coordinated neuro-metabolic interactions during tissue repair. Together, our findings demonstrate the importance of riboflavin metabolism for nervous system regeneration and provide new insight into the spatial organization of metabolism during tissue regeneration.

items.title: Intranasal L-MYC Neural Stem Cells Restore Neurovascular and Neuroimmune Homeostasis After TBI via CX3CL1 Upregulation and ICAM-1 Downregulation
items.abstract_or_text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers persistent neuroimmune and neurovascular dysfunction that contributes to secondary brain injury and limits recovery. Here, we investigated whether a single intranasal dose of LMNSC01 could reprogram neuroinflammatory and neurovascular responses post TBI and whether these effects were conserved across biological sex. Immunocompetent male and female rats underwent a controlled cortical impact (CCI) or Sham surgery and 7 days later received a single bolus dose of LMNSC01 (6 x10^6 cells/dose) or vehicle. Integrated histological and transcriptomic analyses and multiplex tissue ELISA were used to characterize injury- and treatment-associated responses. CCI induced persistent but sex-dependent transcriptional changes. Male rats exhibited prominent innate immune, adhesion, extracellular matrix, and tissue remodeling responses, whereas females demonstrated broader activation of microglial, interferon, complement, MHC/antigen presentation, and humoral/adaptive immune pathways. LMNSC01 treatment reprogrammed these distinct injury states through partially sex-specific mechanisms. In males, LMNSC01 increased endogenous immune-regulatory mediators, including Il1rn, and reduced pathways associated with adhesion and immune cell trafficking. In females, treatment decreased expression of genes related to microglial, leukocyte, MHC/antigen presentation, cytokine, and adhesion pathways, and reduced macrophage- and CD45 positive cell signatures. Despite these sex-dependent transcriptional changes, LMNSC01 produced conserved protein changes in both sexes, reducing injury associated ICAM-1 and restoring CX3CL1 proteins, proposing a novel molecular mechanism of LMNSCs modulating endothelial activation and neuron-microglia communication post injury. Our study provides further insight into sex differences in responses to injury and treatment after TBI and highlights candidate repair mechanisms, supporting further development of LMNSC01 as a minimally invasive therapy for TBI.

items.title: A perturbation atlas of mouse neural organoids resolves macroglial reactivity and nominates drivers of degeneration
items.abstract_or_text: Understanding neuro-glial roles in homeostasis and disease requires scalable central nervous system (CNS) models, particularly as macroglia like astrocytes and Muller glia remain challenging to study in slow-developing human systems. Here, we generate and map the cellular diversity of mouse neural organoids spanning multiple brain regions and the retina. Benchmarking transcriptomic maturation against in vivo references captures postnatal neuro-macroglial states within a month. We show that macroglia are highly responsive to inflammatory cues and adopt specific transcriptomic states also found in vivo. Through a single-cell perturbation screen targeting 13 Muller-glia-specific pathways, we map how certain inflammatory cytokines drive degeneration-like stress programs in photoreceptors and distinct reactive states in Muller glia, including an Oncostatin M-driven chaperone-associated state. Mechanistically, we identify gp130-STAT3 signaling as a targetable driver of macroglial reactivity and photoreceptor distress. Together, these single-cell atlases provide a foundation for dissecting cellular crosstalk and neuro-glial pathology in the mature CNS.

items.title: Collapsing Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis Progression to ESRD Following Combination Therapy with Pembrolizumab and Enfortumab Vedotin: A Case Report
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Introduction: Pembrolizumab (PB), a PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor, and enfortumab vedotin (EV), a Nectin-4 targeting antibody-drug conjugate delivering the microtubule-disrupting payload MMAE, represent the current standard of care for advanced urothelial carcinoma. While PB-associated glomerulopathy is a recognized rare complication, rapid one-month progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) following the EV-PB combination has not been previously described. Case Presentation: A 76-year-old male with high-grade urothelial carcinoma and baseline Stage 4 CKD (eGFR 25 mL/min/1.73 m^2, creatinine 2.5 mg/dL) secondary to prior cisplatin exposure was initiated on PB 200 mgIV and EV 1 mg/kg IV on a 21-day cycle. Within one month, he developed AKI presenting with a creatinine of 3.1 mg/dL, eGFR of 20 mL/min/1.73 m^2, and nephrotic-range proteinuria of 13.1 g/24 hours. Renal biopsy confirmed cFSGS with 53% global glomerulosclerosis and 70% cortical fibrosis. Both agents were discontinued, and rituximab was initiated; however, renal function still deteriorated. Six months later he presented with labs of: creatinine 8.4 mg/dL, eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m^2; requiring emergent hemodialysis. Renal function did not recover, and the patient progressed to permanent ESRD. Discussion/Conclusion: This case highlights three key teaching points. First, pre-existing CKD from prior nephrotoxic chemotherapy amplifies the risk of irreversible cFSGS progression following ADC-immunotherapy, underscoring the need for baseline nephrology evaluation in this population. Second, we propose a novel synergistic mechanism whereby PB-induced podocyte dedifferentiation and cell-cycle re-entry renders those podocytes selectively vulnerable to MMAE-mediated cytotoxicity which can potentially explain the unusually rapid deterioration observed. Third, once advanced interstitial fibrosis is established, immunosuppressive salvage is unlikely to alter the trajectory, and its toxicity must be weighed against a negligible probability of benefit. Notably, PB-induced cFSGS typically remits within 2–3 months of drug discontinuation; however, the literature on dual therapy with EV remains limited.

items.title: Histone H2A.X contributes to Gene Expression Regulation and Cell-Cycle Progression in Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoites
items.abstract_or_text: Histone H2A.X is a conserved variant classically associated with the DNA damage response (DDR), where its phosphorylation ({gamma}H2A.X) marks double-strand breaks and recruits repair factors. H2A.X is absent in many parasitic protozoans such as Plasmodium, Trypanosoma and Leishmania. In Toxoplasma gondii, the obligate intracellular parasite, causative agent of toxoplasmosis, however, its presence raises the question of whether it contributes to genome stability. To tackle this, we generated a T. gondii knockout of H2A.X (RH{Delta}H2A.X) and evaluated its phenotype. Although H2A.X is phosphorylated in response to DNA damage in T. gondii as in other systems, RH{Delta}H2A.X parasites showed no increased sensitivity to genotoxic agents, indicating that H2A.X is dispensable for canonical DDR. Instead, loss of H2A.X caused reduced gliding motility, increased host cell invasion and clustering of extracellular parasites after egress. Despite no defects in replication rate, RH{Delta}H2A.X showed delayed mitotic progression with abnormal vacuole morphology. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a moderate yet coordinated reprogramming of protein-coding genes. Specifically, H2A.X loss altered the expression of key apical secretory and virulence factors, especially ROP18, while inducing the transcriptional activation of mitotic and DNA replication machinery. Differential enrichment analysis further revealed that upregulated genes were preferentially associated with S phase, whereas downregulated genes were enriched during mitosis and cytokinesis. This is consistent with the delayed mitotic progression and spindle abnormalities observed by microscopy and flow cytometry and suggests a cell cycle phase-specific mechanism of H2A.X-dependent transcriptional control. Rather than a driver of DDR, these findings suggest that T. gondii H2A.X operates as a chromatin organizer that coordinates cell division fidelity and virulence gene expression.

items.title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Clinical foundation models learn patterns in longitudinal health records that can be reused across prediction tasks. However, the relative strengths of representation-based and generation-based prediction across clinical tasks remain unclear. Using longitudinal electronic health records from 3.77 million patients at a single hospital, we developed FERMAT (Foundation model for Exploring Real-world Multimodal health data using Autoregressive Trajectory modeling), a 65-million-parameter clinical foundation model. We compared predictions from task-specific predictors trained on patient representations with those derived from generated clinical event sequences. Representation-based prediction performed better in the disease-risk comparisons. In detailed analyses of five-year chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, and diabetes risk in a test cohort of 10,000 patients, representation-based predictors exceeded generation-based estimates by 0.098-0.115 in observation-weighted AUROC and had lower probability error. Generation-based prediction, in turn, performed better in predicting diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures recorded on the same day, a task motivated by the frequent presence of multiple events with the same date in hospital EHRs. Using 50 generated trajectories per patient, it achieved a Recall@10 of 71.0%, compared with 55.7% for representation-based prediction, with a paired improvement of 15.31 percentage points (95% CI, 13.92-16.79; n = 1,862). These findings demonstrate task-dependent strengths of representation-based and generation-based applications within a single clinical foundation model, providing an empirical basis for exploring how the two approaches can be used individually or combined to address clinical prediction needs.

items.title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
items.abstract_or_text: Decision models like Jev read text and return probabilities, categories, or ordinal levels, with confidence scores for the latter two, at a fraction of large language models' (LLMs) cost. We explored how Jev could be integrated into clinical workflows for all these output types: mortality risk estimation, categorical Choosing-Wisely decisions for patient questions, and ordinal colon cancer staging. With standard LLM-style inputs, Jev trailed five flagship LLMs: mortality AUROC was 0.822 versus 0.837-0.846; Choosing-Wisely accuracy, 87.7% versus 98.4-100%; and staging accuracy, 45.4% versus 94.2-100%. Developer-recommended input alterations improved staging accuracy to 75.8% with medical context, 82.1% with task decomposition, and 85.8% with both. None of Jev's staging errors had full confidence. Using Jev for fully confident staging decisions and LLMs for the rest was non-inferior to each LLM alone and cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44%. Prompted as designed, decision models may efficiently share structured clinical tasks with LLMs.

items.title: Intracellular accumulation of AAV6 genomes governs microglia reactivity and the inflammatory response in retinal gene therapy
items.abstract_or_text: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors possess immense potential for gene therapy applications. However, microglia can mount an immune response against AAV vectors. Yet, microglia are therapeutic targets since they play a driving role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, it is critical to understand the cellular processes driving the microglia-mediated immune response against AAV vectors. To this end, we modelled AAV6 induced inflammation upon retinal gene therapy in minipigs. Upon AAV6 administration, the IBA1+ cells demonstrated a morphological transition to the amoeboid form, indicating microglial reactivity. We also observed the invasion of peripheral immune cells in the retina. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, we transduced human iPSC derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) in vitro with AAV6 and AAV8 respectively. Only AAV6 transduced iMGLs exhibited morphological features and a transcriptomic signature of microglial reactivity. The magnitude of intracellular AAV6 viral genomes was significantly higher as compared to the AAV8 condition. The elevated levels of intracellular AAV6 genomes induced a DNA damage response in AAV6-transduced iMGLs, which is a key feature of neuroinflammation-linked microglial reactivity. Thus, our work highlights the impact of intracellular viral genome accumulation on microglial reactivity and its implications for retinal gene therapy associated inflammation.

items.title: Lineage tracing reveals asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos and stem cell-derived embryo models
items.abstract_or_text: How a flexible mammalian embryo gives rise to a reproducible body plan remains unclear, partly because cell lineages cannot be followed continuously in vivo. We combined DNA Typewriter lineage recording with tetraploid complementation to reconstruct high-resolution single-cell genealogies across mouse development and built FateVec, an analysis framework that infers fate-bias dynamics and lineage-associated transcriptional programs from reconstructed phylogenies. Loss of developmental potential proved progressive and asynchronous, with multiple lineages acquiring detectable fate bias before morphological diversification at gastrulation. Within the neural crest, most cells remained multipotent over an extended window, while independent founder clades differed markedly in restriction timing. Extending lineage recording to a stem-cell-derived embryo model revealed that cells with shared transcriptional identities can arise from distinct lineage relationships. We further found embryonic-lineage contributions to extraembryonic-like states, exposing an unexplored lineage plasticity. This lineage-resolved view of embryogenesis reveals that cell identity alone predicts neither developmental ancestry nor the timing of fate restriction.

items.title: Inherent limitations of zero-shot mutation prediction in protein engineering
items.abstract_or_text: Predicting mutation effects is critical for protein engineering. A commonly pursued strategy is zero-shot prediction with deep-learning models, whose performance is typically evaluated using aggregate benchmark scores that obscure multidimensional biological tradeoffs. Here, we evaluate sequence, structure, and hybrid foundation models across curated datasets to expose the practical limitations of zero-shot predictions. We demonstrate that model performance is highly variable and heavily influenced by experimental noise and competing phenotypic goals. Notably, predictions from competing models often correlate more strongly with one another than with experimental outcomes. While current models effectively filter deleterious mutations and enrich high-scoring variants for natural functions, they struggle to identify precise optimal mutations and consistently fail to predict mutations that drive new-to-nature functions. These models learn from evolutionary constraints that tend to oppose the extreme biophysical optimizations required in targeted engineering. Consequently, zero-shot scoring serves as a valuable initial filter but cannot substitute for task-specific prediction.

items.title: Development of a nanomedicine approach to improve the therapeutic index of bexarotene.
items.abstract_or_text: Bexarotene (BEX), a retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases and inflammatory conditions, including multiple sclerosis (MS). However, its broader clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, and dose-limiting adverse effects, most notably hypertriglyceridaemia. In this study, we investigated whether conjugation of BEX to dextrin, a biodegradable polysaccharide, could improve its physicochemical properties and therapeutic index. A dextrin-BEX conjugate was synthesised using succinoylated dextrin (30 mol%) and characterised by gel permeation chromatography (GPC), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) and dynamic light scattering (DLS). The effects of conjugation on solubility, aggregation behaviour and biological activity were evaluated using in vitro cytotoxicity assays in leukaemia, liver and fibroblast cell lines, alongside measurements of intracellular triglyceride levels. The impact on lipid metabolism and toxicity was further assessed in an in vivo murine model of hyperlipidaemia. Dextrin conjugation significantly increased the aqueous solubility of BEX (from <0.004 mg/mL to 9.88 mg/mL) and led to the formation of nanoscale aggregates in solution. This was associated with a marked increase in in vitro potency, with IC50 values reduced by up to 14-fold across multiple cell lines. However, the increased cytotoxicity was not selective for cancer cells and was also observed in normal fibroblast and hepatic cell models. The dextrin-BEX conjugate did not induce intracellular triglyceride accumulation in vitro. In vivo, dextrin conjugation did not mitigate BEX-associated lipid dysregulation, while serum triglyceride levels and markers of liver injury remained unchanged. However, although free BEX led to a significant increase in liver weight after 14 days, the dextrin-BEX conjugate did not produce a statistically significant effect. In conclusion, dextrin conjugation markedly improves the solubility and in vitro potency of BEX but does not enhance its selectivity or reduce its metabolic toxicity in vivo. These findings suggest that while polymer conjugation is an effective strategy for addressing physicochemical limitations, it is insufficient to overcome the inherent dyslipidaemia associated with systemic RXR activation. Future strategies should focus on integrating targeting and controlled release mechanisms, alongside approaches that address the underlying pharmacological drivers of lipid dysregulation.

items.title: Human Metalloenzymes Are Disproportionately Linked to Disease: The HEAM Structural Annotation Resource
items.abstract_or_text: Catalytic metal-binding sites are established drug targets for many human diseases, yet systematic study of how metal function relates to disease is limited by the lack of a resource combining structural localization of human metal-binding sites with catalytic annotation at scale. We introduce HEAM (the Human Enzymatic Annotation of Metalloproteins), a structurally annotated dataset of 1,933 human metalloenzymes and 1,171 non-catalytic metalloproteins. HEAM incorporates annotated metals into protein structures at their corresponding binding sites and classifies each site as catalytic or non-catalytic using the machine learning classifier MAHOMES II. HEAM more than quadruples the human site-level coverage of the largest prior metalloenzyme database. Using HEAM, we show that human metalloproteins are significantly enriched in KEGG disease pathways relative to the human proteome, and that metalloenzymes specifically are significantly enriched in ClinVar pathogenic variants -- a distinction obscured in prior, catalytically unresolved metalloprotein datasets. These pathogenic variants are concentrated in metabolic disorders, indicating that metabolic dysfunction is a substantial contributor to metalloenzyme-linked disease. By pairing 3D structural annotation with catalytic classification, HEAM provides both a foundation for structure-guided drug design against metal-binding sites and a resource for determining how catalytic and non-catalytic metal function contribute to human disease.

items.title: Subtype-Selective Neuronal Vulnerability and Compensatory Neuroglial Remodeling in Human Cortical Dementia
items.abstract_or_text: Whether the nodal vulnerability in dementia is solely represented by changes in cellular abundance or attrition of cellular transcriptomic landscape attribute to that transition in aging brain is yet to uncover with minutiae. To understand this complication, we have analyzed two snRNA-seq data specific to (I) dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC): A comprehensive study of cellular profiling among cognitively normal and pathological ageing and dementia (AD) brain, (II) occipital cortex (OC) in the context of Nasu-Hakola disease along with a tissue level bulk RNA-seq data corresponds to temporal cortex. We pinpoint cellular subpopulations their proportional changes within the nodal points and their transcriptomic profiling. In DLPFC we observed alteration of mitochondrial and synaptic maintenance program in the pathological manifestation of disease. In OC we noticed depleted upper layer CUX2 neuron, PVALB and SST neurons on the contrary an enrichment of RORB and LAMP5 neurons with compromised metabolic states in the disease context. Glial populations are marked by representation of fibrous astrocyte, neuronal-supporting subpopulations associated with extracellular matrix remodeling programs. Proportional increment of intermediate myelinating oligodendrocyte and a decrease in mature myelinating subpopulation highlighted a compromised myelin repair attempt. In temporal cortex at tissue level we observed transcriptomic landscape adopted a neuroglial phenotypes in dementia brain. Cell-Chat analysis demonstrated a shift in cellular coordination towards glial population from neuron in NHD brain. A single cell-based drug reprofiling approach identified efatutazone and balaglitazone as broad-spectrum candidates for major cell types in occipital cortex, whereas major actionable biological targets belong to CDK subtypes and proteasome subunits. Overall, our findings imply cellular persistence do not necessarily substantiate molecular preservation, also the coexistence of cellular vulnerability alongside selective remodeling features, present a cellular framework on how to cope up with degenerative changes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Tooth Numbering and Full-Mouth Series Placement
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract This study proposes an automated method for detecting tooth positions and predicting full-mouth series (FMS) radiograph placement using oriented object detection and Siamese neural networks. A total of 5,431 radiographs from 354 patients were annotated and used to train deep learning models. Oriented bounding boxes were generated using a YOLOv5 detector, followed by tooth numbering, feature extraction, and image classification via a multitask ResNet50 model. FMS placement was predicted using a Siamese neural network inspired by jigsaw-puzzle tasks, with permutation-based training and patient-level five-fold cross-validation. Mean tooth-numbering accuracy was 0.99 ± 0.00. Mean FMS-placement accuracy was 0.97 ± 0.01 for upper left and right periapical radiographs, 0.98 ± 0.02 for upper anterior periapical radiographs, 0.98 ± 0.01 for lower left and right periapical radiographs, 0.99 ± 0.01 for lower anterior periapical radiographs, and 0.96 ± 0.02 for bitewing radiographs; overall mean accuracy was 0.98 ± 0.01. This internally tested AI pipeline demonstrated high accuracy for tooth numbering and automated FMS arrangement and may help streamline dental radiographic workflows, subject to external and clinical validation.

items.title: Assessing User-Subjective Experience with Conversational Agents for Behavioral and Mental Health Interventions: Design and Psychometric Evaluation of CUE-Chat
items.abstract_or_text: While AI-conversational agents are increasingly integrated into behavioral and mental health interventions, standardized instruments to assess their performance remain scarce. To address this gap, we developed an instrument to measure user-subjective experience with AI-driven agents in the healthcare domain. We focused on user perception due to its direct contribution to intervention effects, and on healthcare given that the rapid adoption of AI-agents in this domain continues to outpace the development of validated evaluation instruments. Across four studies, we developed and tested the Chatbot User Evaluation instrument (CUE-Chat). First, we identified relevant assessment domains and items through literature review, existing instruments, input from AI-driven agents, and the research team’s domain expertise. Following this, we requested feedback on draft subscales, definitions, and items from expert and laypeople panels. We then tested the structure of the instrument’s concept version. Finally, we conducted a psychometric evaluation and finalized the instrument.CUE-Chat consists of four factors: Perceived Efficacy (4 items), Usability (4 items), Intelligence (4 items), and Safety and Risk Management (4 items). Reliability and validity of the total score and each subscale was good to excellent (Cronbach’s α = .73-.92; Ω = .74-.93). Predictive validity was strong with all scales predictive of users’ overall rating of an AI-agent’s performance.We conclude that CUE-Chat’s strong psychometric properties are promising, and that it is particularly useful for researchers integrating AI-driven agents into behavioral and mental health interventions in both developmental and evaluative stages.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Clinical, Laboratory, and Chest CT Features Between COVID-19 and H1N1 Pneumonia: A Large-Scale Retrospective Study with Machine Learning Integration
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Concurrent COVID-19 and influenza A(H1N1) epidemics since late 2019 have complicated early differentiation because of overlapping clinical and imaging features. Viral evolution, shifting population immunity, and emerging variants may have altered imaging phenotypes, underscoring the need for contemporary data. We aimed to compare clinical, laboratory, and CT characteristics between COVID-19 and H1N1 pneumonia, identify independent predictors for each diagnosis, and explore machine learning (ML) models for differentiation. Methods This retrospective study included 612 patients (442 H1N1, 170 COVID-19) diagnosed between January 2023 and December 2025. Clinical, laboratory, and chest CT features were comprehensively analyzed. Between-group differences were assessed by χ² test or Mann-Whitney U test. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify the independent predictive factors. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for feature selection. Five ML algorithms were trained (70% of cohort) and tested (30%). Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Parenchymal involvement was more frequent in COVID-19 than in H1N1 pneumonia (91.2% vs 74.7%; P 0.001), with higher rates of ground‑glass opacities, interlobular septal thickening, and crazy-paving pattern. Airway involvement was more frequent in H1N1 pneumonia (48.2% vs 34.7%; P = 0.003), including higher rates of bronchial wall thickening, centrilobular nodules, and tree‑in‑bud nodules. On multivariable analysis, upper lobe involvement (OR = 2.19; 95% CI: 1.04, 4.65) and parenchymal involvement (OR = 3.44; 95% CI: 1.67, 7.10) were independent predictors of COVID-19. Tree-in-bud nodules (OR = 0.30; 95% CI: 0.12, 0.77), lymphadenopathy (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.81), and disorders of consciousness (OR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.07, 0.61) were independently associated with H1N1 pneumonia. Among five ML models, the random forest model achieved the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.71 (95% CI: 0.58, 0.85) for differentiation. Conclusion Upper lobe involvement and parenchymal involvement are independent predictors of COVID-19, whereas tree-in-bud nodules, lymphadenopathy, and disorders of consciousness are independently associated with H1N1 pneumonia. These imaging and clinical features may facilitate early differential diagnosis.

items.title: Probable neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease in an Asian woman without detectable NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion on routine testing
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder characterized by eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions. GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC is strongly associated with adult-onset NIID in East Asian populations. Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS), associated with an FMR1 CGG premutation, can overlap with NIID clinically, radiologically, and pathologically. Negative targeted repeat-expansion results therefore require interpretation alongside clinicopathological findings. Case presentation: A 67-year-old Asian woman with no known family history of neurological disease developed progressive cognitive decline in 2021, followed by limb ataxia and bilateral lower-limb weakness. In 2025, her ADL and mRS scores were 51/56 and 3; MoCA and MMSE scores were 8/30 and 19/30. Electrophysiological findings suggested predominantly motor demyelinating polyneuropathy. Brain MRI showed bilateral corticomedullary-junction hyperintensities on DWI and confluent periventricular and deep white-matter abnormalities on FLAIR and T2WI. A skin biopsy obtained above the lateral malleolus showed eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in sweat gland epithelial cells and fibroblasts, with positive SQSTM1/p62 and SUMO1 immunostaining. RP-PCR did not detect a NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion. Both FMR1 alleles were reported to contain 29 CGG repeats, below the premutation range. During 14 months of follow-up, no impaired consciousness, seizures, or encephalopathy-like episodes occurred, and the mRS Scale score remained 3. Cognitive scores changed in opposite directions, precluding conclusions about cognitive change or treatment response. The clinical, radiological, and previously reported pathological findings supported probable NIID, apparently sporadic, without molecular confirmation. Conclusions: Characteristic MRI and skin biopsy findings remain diagnostically informative when routine NOTCH2NLC screening detects no expansion. FMR1 analysis aids differentiation from FXTAS. A negative targeted result alone should neither exclude NIID nor imply a novel causative gene; confirmation using an independent repeat-expansion assay or long-read sequencing should be considered when available.

items.title: HERO: A hierarchy-aware analysis pipeline for reducing and refining whole-brain atlas-mapped cellular datasets
items.abstract_or_text: Advances in high-throughput mesoscale microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis pipelines have made unbiased whole-brain imaging widely accessible. However, translating the resulting atlas-mapped datasets into biologically meaningful results remains a substantial barrier owing to their sheer magnitude and complex hierarchical organization. Consequently, reporting structure and analysis methods vary widely across studies, undermining rigor and reproducibility. To address this, we developed a user-friendly data reduction workflow, HERO (Hierarchy-aware Expression Region Organization), designed to perform hierarchy-aware selection, refinement, ranking, and visualization of whole-brain cell detection datasets. The workflow is customizable to specific needs, requires minimal coding experience, and outputs transparent, curated results. HERO functions as a seamless plug-in within larger-scale whole-brain cell detection analysis pipelines, providing efficient, unbiased region selection to streamline subsequent statistical analyses and comparative evaluations. Although HERO is developed with mouse cell-detection datasets, it can be applied to any atlas-mapped dataset that contains hierarchical information. Here, we applied the HERO pipeline to example cell detection datasets containing afferent cells from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BST) and the insular cortex (insula). HERO provided top projecting regions consistent with historical tracing studies for the BST (e.g., amygdalar and hypothalamic regions) and the insula (e.g., somatosensory, autonomic, and interoceptive regions). Furthermore, the refinement step of HERO provides additional enriched regions originally obscured in the primary ranked outputs, such as memory- and emotion-associated structures. With HEROs dynamic processing, we were able to identify top-projecting regions consistent with the literature and, additionally, find regions often obscured in these large datasets. In sum, HERO offers a standardized analysis workflow to reduce whole-brain cell-detection datasets, transforming raw regional cell counts into curated results and advancing the effectiveness, interpretability, and accessibility of whole-brain imaging in neuroscience.

items.title: Towards Robust Automated Mouse Scratching Behavior Detection for Itch Research
items.abstract_or_text: Automated detection of mouse scratching behavior could reduce manual annotation and is essential for preclinical itch research. However, robust performance across laboratories remains a challenge for current methods. We present Scratch-AID+, a framework dedicated to automated mouse scratching detection, including a diverse and progressive set of approaches: classic ResNet-based detectors, task-adaptive fine-tuning of video foundation models, and in-context learning with advanced multimodal large language models. To simulate real-world use cases, we benchmark on a public dataset and utilize additional cross-laboratory video recordings for independent testing. We find that classic baselines suffered severe performance degradation on external data under the realistic setting with sparse scratching events. In contrast, fine-tuned video foundation models successfully bridged this generalizability gap, achieving significantly better detection performance. Furthermore, frozen multimodal large language models demonstrated promising out-of-the-box ability using only few-shot demonstrations. We also examined the effects of different video preprocessing strategies. Our findings highlight the improved performance and generalizability of the adapted foundation models for automated scratching behavior analysis and shed light on the real-world deployment of such detectors. Our code is publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/scratch aid-plus/.

items.title: Cell Painting and machine learning for mechanistic profiling of hepatotoxic botanicals and their constituents
items.abstract_or_text: BACKGROUND Botanicals are widely consumed as herbal remedies and plant-derived products, but their complex and variable chemical composition presents major challenges for safety assessment. Although hepatotoxicity has been reported for several botanicals, the constituent compounds responsible and the underlying mechanisms often remain poorly characterised. OBJECTIVES We aimed to determine whether Cell Painting could identify candidate constituent drivers of botanical bioactivity and generate hypotheses about potential mechanisms of action in primary human hepatocytes. METHODS We profiled 13 botanical extracts and 85 known constituents across multiple concentrations using Cell Painting alongside assays of metabolic activity and membrane integrity. To interpret morphological phenotypes, we trained machine-learning models using a Cell Painting reference atlas of >1,000 chemicals linked to ToxCast/Tox21 molecular and cellular bioactivity annotations.
