RESULTS Cell Painting detected bioactivity in 11/13 botanical extracts and 46/85 constituents, compared with 9/13 extracts and 40/85 constituents in the cell-health assays, and generally detected activity at lower concentrations. For 9/13 extracts, at least one constituent was active at a lower concentration than the corresponding botanical extract, supporting the contribution of a subset of potent constituents to mixture-level responses. Aristolochia and goldenseal were the most potent extracts across Cell Painting and cell-health assays and contained highly active constituents. Reference-atlas models generated specific mechanistic hypotheses, including cytotoxicity-, endocrine-, and genotoxicity-associated responses for several botanicals and constituents. CONCLUSION These results support Cell Painting combined with machine learning as a sensitive approach for characterising cellular responses to botanicals, prioritising candidate constituent drivers of hepatotoxicity-associated phenotypes, and generating testable hypotheses about potential mechanisms of action.

items.title: tRNAZAP: Deep learning toolkit for nanopore tRNA signal analysis
items.abstract_or_text: tRNA are short, ~76 nucleotide-long, modification-rich molecules that play an important role in protein translation. Nanopore sequencing is the only platform capable of directly sequencing full-length, native tRNA molecules. This capability is enabled by splinted ligation of tRNA-specific adapters. As a result, the measured ionic current signal reflects a composition of both adapter and tRNA sequence features. Despite these advantages, analysis of nanopore tRNA sequencing data poses distinct computational challenges. Existing ionic current-based signal-to-sequence decoding (basecalling) models are optimized for mRNA and perform suboptimally on short, modification-dense RNA such as tRNA. Furthermore, alignment algorithms for reference-guided analysis of short-length reads are not optimized for nanopore reads with lower accuracy than Next-generation sequencing reads. To overcome these limitations, domain-specific computational approaches are required. We present tRNAZAP, a nanopore ionic current signal analysis toolkit designed to enable precise reference-guided sequence alignment. tRNAZAP operates directly on raw ionic current signals and decomposes the analysis into two complementary tasks: 1) segmentation of adapter and tRNA regions, and 2) tRNA classification, both implemented using transformer-based models. The segmentation component isolates the tRNA signal portion and extracts the corresponding nucleotide sequence as the alignment query, while the classification component identifies the tRNA type as the alignment reference without requiring sequence-level information. Together, these outputs allow direct optimal pairwise alignment between the tRNA subsequence of the full query and reference sequences. Trained on in vitro transcribed RNA data and evaluated on yeast tRNA, these models achieved ~98% classification accuracy and intersection-over-union of ~0.98 for segmentation.

items.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
items.abstract_or_text: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates secondary neurodegeneration that compromises interconnected neural circuits and contributes to persistent visual and neurobehavioral impairment. Pharmacological strategies that preserve vulnerable neurons and synapses while limiting chronic neuroinflammation remain an unmet therapeutic need. We previously identified the serotonin 1A receptor (5-HT1A) antagonist WAY-100635 through screening human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and demonstrated that it promotes neuroprotection through cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis. Here, we investigated whether post-injury treatment extends this neuroprotective efficacy to cerebral and visual circuitry following TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice aged 2-3 months underwent unilateral controlled cortical impact (CCI) involving the left visual cortex. Mice were randomly assigned to sham, untreated injury or treated injury groups, with 3-10 sham controls and 5-8 mice per injury group across experiments. WAY-100635 was administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg daily, beginning 1 hour after injury and continuing for 6 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed using motor and psychological-health-relevant risk-taking/behavioral disinhibition by elevated-plus-maze assessment, visual electrophysiology, optokinetic responses, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, and retinal and cortical histopathology. Unilateral cortical injury produced bilateral RGC dysfunction and loss, with greater degeneration in the eye contralateral to the injured hemisphere, consistent with predominantly crossed murine visual projections. WAY-100635 significantly preserved RGC survival and function, improved visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, and preserved visually evoked cortical responses to contralateral eye stimulation. Diffusion MRI revealed bilateral visual pathway abnormalities, with treatment selectively normalizing fractional anisotropy and radial kurtosis in the optic tract ipsilateral to cortical injury. In perilesional cortex, treatment preserved neuronal cell bodies and synapses detected by synaptophysin immunoreactivity while markedly reducing microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis. These effects were accompanied by improved early motor performance and attenuation of injury-associated increases in open-arm exploration in the elevated plus maze. Cortical cavity volume was not significantly reduced, supporting preferential protection of vulnerable circuitry surrounding and connected to the primary lesion. These findings identify post-injury WAY-100635 treatment as a novel therapeutic intervention that combines neuronal and synaptic preservation with reduced chronic glial activation and improved functional outcomes. They support further translational development of serotonin 1A receptor antagonism to limit secondary neurodegeneration and the visual and neurobehavioral consequences of TBI.

items.title: AnnZarro: scalable, interactive exploration of cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships in single-cell data
items.abstract_or_text: Cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships, such as kernels and correlations, shape most single-cell analyses but are rarely inspected directly due to a lack of visualization tools that display them. AnnZarro is a point-and-click browser viewer that shows these matrices linked to an AnnData object's cells x genes data. Using AnnZarro, experimental biologists can explore data without code and computational biologists can probe the relationships behind their analyses. One focused cell and one focused gene drive every panel. Clicking a cell paints its row of any cell-by-cell matrix over an embedding or spatial coordinates; clicking a gene paints its row of any gene-by-gene matrix over a gene plot such as a volcano. The focus also links genes to the cells where they change, and cells to the genes that distinguish them. AnnZarro reads only the matrix rows and columns each panel displays from zarr stores and hence users can explore matrices far larger than memory on a laptop or a shared server. Large datasets open on a reproducible subset, and users step through the remaining cells in parts. On a laptop, a 100,000-cell part of Tahoe-100M opens in 4 s and stays interactive. With the subset switched off, AnnZarro draws all 95.6 million cells in one plot in about 5 to 7 s. This tutorial prepares a dataset with Kompot differential abundance and expression, a diffusion kernel and gene correlations, then explores it in six worked examples.

items.title: The Roads Not Taken: The Neural Dynamics of Lexical Alternatives During Free Language Production
items.abstract_or_text: Human language allows multiple ways to express the same thought, raising the possibility that several lexical candidates are activated in parallel before a single word is selected for articulation. While their co-activation is assumed by computational models of word production, until recently, there has been no practical way to estimate the identity of these candidates in unconstrained speech, nor to directly probe their representation in neural activity. Here, we combined high-density electrocorticography recorded during real-world conversation with context-sensitive large language model (LLM) to characterize, for the first time, how these lexical candidates are represented in the brain. We focus on the candidates which remain unsaid, referred to as the "alternatives", by only using samples where the LLM predictions do not include the produced word. We provide evidence for three computational principles of the neural dynamics of lexical alternatives: (1) multiple lexical alternatives to each word in conversation are distinctly represented in neural activity prior to articulation; (2) the set of lexical alternatives is rapidly updated from one word to the next; and (3) alternatives to future words are represented along with alternatives to the upcoming word. Together, these findings reveal that spontaneous speech production is supported by a broad, dynamically evolving and forward-looking set of lexical alternatives, providing a neural account of how the brain prepares not only the words that are spoken, but also those that remain unsaid.

items.title: WHITE-Net : White matter HyperIntensities Tissue Extraction using deep learning Network
items.abstract_or_text: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a hallmark of cerebral small vessel disease, a highly prevalent condition in aging, making their accurate detection in large-scale magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies critically important. Currently available semi-automated and automated segmentation methods are frequently limited by sensitivity to variations in imaging conditions and computational constraints, restricting their applicability across diverse acquisition settings. We present WHITE-Net, a deep learning-based framework for automated WMH segmentation built on a 3D ResUNet architecture and trained on multisite MRI data encompassing substantial variability in scanner vendors, acquisition protocols, spatial resolution, and image characteristics. Evaluated across three independent datasets - BrainLaus, ADNI, and WMH Challenge, WHITE-Net achieves high segmentation accuracy and ranks among the top-performing methods across datasets, enabling a comprehensive assessment of generalisability in varied imaging environments. WHITE-Net maintains stable performance in a wide spectrum of lesion loads and demonstrates a favorable balance between precision and recall, effectively limiting false positive detections - a common limitation of existing approaches. Beyond accuracy, WHITE-Net requires no parameter tuning and offers fast inference times, making it well-suited for deployment in large-scale neuroimaging studies. The obtained results highlight the value of training on diverse multisite data for improving generalisability and position WHITE-Net as a reliable, scalable tool for automated WMH segmentation in computational anatomy research.

items.title: From APTs to advanced persistent biological threats (APBTs): a taxonomy and large-scale metadata audit of genomic surveillance infrastructure
items.abstract_or_text: Open genomic repositories have become critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making. However, many of these repositories were designed to support rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification, creating potential security gaps. This paper introduces Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs), as a framework for understanding how malicious cyber biological actors can gradually disrupt genomic surveillance without entering a laboratory or releasing a biological agent. Instead of altering biological material, an attacker targets the sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models used by surveillance systems. We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and investigate whether the metadata weaknesses identified by this framework are present in an operational genomic repository. To assess this, we audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 BioSample records obtained from the NCBI. A framework of 23 checks was applied across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance, and technical metadata. Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata vulnerability indicator, with a mean of 7.34 indicators per record (SD = 1.34). Overall, 97.3% of records were classified in the High or Critical severity categories. Every record also contained at least one indicator in both the provenance and technical metadata layers. These results largely reflect the optional status of several fields in the current BioSample submission model rather than isolated errors by individual data contributors. Temporal and geographic information was comparatively complete, while fields needed for provenance reconstruction, chain of custody assessment, technical validation, and analytical interpretation were frequently missing. These findings do not indicate deliberate manipulation. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance. The findings therefore show that widely used pathogen genomic repositories already contain structural weaknesses that can support metadata poisoning as part of an APBT operation.

items.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning models for electroencephalography (EEG) pathology detection achieve competitive accuracy but offer limited interpretability. In this paper, we introduce concept bottleneck models (CBMs) for EEG pathology detection which use clinical EEG biomarkers computed analytically from the signal as a bottleneck to be used for prediction. Those concepts include band power, spectral ratios, alpha peak frequency and amplitude, hemispheric asymmetry and phase locking values. With the backbone based on shallow convolutional neural network (CNN), we compare a black box baseline with two variants of CBMs. The hybrid variant is a classifier receives a residual projection of the backbone features. The pure variant is a CBM where the classifier receives only the predicted concepts. Models are evaluated on abnormality detection and dementia classification followed by concept prediction quality and leakage analysis. Both CBMs approach the baseline on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) and are 2-5 percentage points lower on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%). The pure CBM exhibits concept fidelity concern where the predicted concepts deviate from their ground truth values. Replacing them with their true values causes severe cost on accuracy by 26 and 22 points on TUAB and CAUEEG. The concept fidelity concern is mitigated by increasing the weight of the concept loss to match the ground truth concepts. the mitigation comes with small accuracy cost on TUAB but a relatively larger cost on CAUEEG. The code of the experiments and full logs are available at https://www.github.com/mhmdrdwn/cbm.

items.title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Machine Learning (ML) has shown promise in histopathological diagnosis, but rare tumours, like duodenal epithelial neoplasms, are challenging because large, labelled datasets are difficult to assemble. We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. Methods: We assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. Results: In leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. Conclusions: We present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

items.title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study
items.abstract_or_text: Tissue-based assays provide broad screening for neural autoantibodies but remain vulnerable to technical and reader-dependent variability. We evaluated an integrated workflow combining automated 3,3'-diaminobenzidine tissue-based assay processing, digital whole-slide imaging, and interpretable deep learning. Model development used 2,357 retrospective serum and cerebrospinal fluid images referred from more than 80 institutions and processed in a centralized laboratory, with reference labels established by expert-consensus tissue-based assay interpretation. A prospective validation cohort included 200 images from 200 unique patients (154 positive and 46 negative; 100 serum and 100 cerebrospinal fluid). The same images were evaluated by two expert and two novice readers in a fixed-order two-round study, with unaided interpretation followed by artificial-intelligence-assisted interpretation after a washout of at least two weeks. The standalone binary classifier achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.922, accuracy of 86.5%, sensitivity of 85.7%, and specificity of 89.1% in prospective validation. Pooled reader accuracy was 90.4% in the unaided round and 97.4% in the artificial-intelligence-assisted round (McNemar P < 0.001), with specificity of 82.6% and 99.5%, respectively. Novice-reader accuracy was 83.3% unaided and 96.5% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001), approaching unaided expert accuracy of 97.5%. Among tissue-based-assay-positive cases, reader accuracy for cytoplasmic/nuclear antigen-associated versus neural surface antigen-associated staining-pattern subclassification was 88.8% unaided and 94.0% with artificial-intelligence assistance (P < 0.001). These findings support further multicentre, cross-platform evaluation of artificial-intelligence-assisted neural autoantibody tissue interpretation.

items.title: From examinations to consultations: a physician-reviewed Japanese benchmark for large language models in traditional Kampo medicine
items.abstract_or_text: Objectives: Patients and clinicians increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) about Kampo, Japan's traditional medicine. Yet evaluations of LLMs have measured accuracy on examination questions, which ask what a model knows; a consultation asks whether it can apply that knowledge to the patient at hand. No benchmark had measured that. Materials and Methods: KampoBench comprises 74 consultation scenarios and 310 conversation-specific rubric criteria, following the design of HealthBench. Scenarios, criteria and reference answers were drafted by an LLM and revised by board-certified Kampo physicians. Ten current models from three vendors were evaluated. Because LLM graders are known to favor their own family, each response was graded by a model from each vendor. Results: The best model reached 74.8-86.3% across graders, the physician-revised reference answers 87.9-92.4%. Rankings were stable across graders (Spearman's rho 0.952-0.976), and the family-favoring deviation was 0.4 to 0.6 percentage points, below the bootstrap standard deviation of one measurement; grader leniency varied by 14.3 points. Models were most reliable on criteria about advising that care be sought (83.6%) and least reliable on those requiring a known crude-drug risk to be tied to the case (17.5%), though 79.2% of those responses named the drug. Discussion: The shortfall lay in applying knowledge to the case rather than in holding it - a distinction examination-format evaluations cannot make. Conclusion: Evaluation in traditional medicine should measure the judgments a consultation requires, not recall alone. Quoted alongside the grader that produced it, a KampoBench score is a usable measure of those judgments.

items.title: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning-Based Person and Scene Analysis Using Eye-Reflected Images
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Among the various reflective imaging modalities, eye reflections have emerged as a valuable source of visual information for person and scene analysis. Such imagery can capture contextual and identity-related cues from reflected environments, supporting applications in forensic analysis, biometric recognition, intelligent surveillance, and safety-critical domains. However, analysis of persons and scenes using eye-reflected images remains challenging due to their inherently small spatial extent, optical distortions, motion blur, illumination variability, and limited image resolution. Although machine learning techniques have demonstrated potential in addressing these challenges, existing research remains fragmented across different tasks, approaches, and application domains. While substantial research has investigated face identification and computer vision tasks using direct images, no systematic review has comprehensively synthesised machine learning-based approaches for person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images. This study addresses this gap by critically analysing machine learning techniques for person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images. A total of 12 primary studies, published between January 2006 and August 2026, were systematically identified and selected from Q1 and Q2 journals. The systematic review was conducted in accordance with the guidelines proposed by Kitchenham and Charters and the PRISMA 2020 framework. The review examined eye-reflected image sources, datasets, preprocessing techniques, machine learning models and architectures, analysis tasks, evaluation metrics, and application domains. A taxonomy of machine learning-based person and scene analysis is proposed to organise and synthesise this research area. The review identifies key research gaps and limitations and outlines future research directions to advance person and scene analysis using eye-reflected images.

items.title: Harmine derivative ACB1801 induces ferroptosis vulnerability and STAT1 pathway activation to sensitize MSS colorectal cancer to anti–PD-1 immunotherapy
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Harmine and its derivatives, a class of β-carboline alkaloids, are promising natural antitumor agents with drug resistance–modulating activities. Emerging evidence suggests that these small molecules can reshape the tumor microenvironment (TME) and modulate antitumor immunity. Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies provide durable benefit in a subset of colorectal cancers but remain largely ineffective in microsatellite-stable (MSS) subtype, which accounts for approximately 85% of cases. This lack of response is driven by an immune-desert TME characterized by defective antigen presentation and poor cytotoxic T cell infiltration. Whether harmine derivatives can enhance ICB efficacy in MSS colorectal cancer remains unknown, and the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly defined. We therefore evaluated how ACB1801, a synthetic derivative of the natural harmine, reprograms the TME to restore sensitivity to anti-Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) therapy in MSS CRC. In murine MSS CRC models, ACB1801 markedly enhanced the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1, resulting in increased intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and reduced regulatory T cell accumulation. Integrated transcriptomic analyses of sorted CD45⁺ immune and CD45⁻ tumor compartments revealed that combination therapy induced coordinated metabolic reprogramming, characterized by suppression of glycolysis and activation of ferroptosis-related pathways. These findings were validated in murine and human MSS CRC cell lines, where ACB1801 reduced glycolytic flux and increased ferroptotic susceptibility. Mechanistically, ACB1801 enhanced C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) secretion in a STAT1-dependent manner and upregulated NOD-like receptor family CARD domain containing 5 (NLRC5)-driven MHC class I antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor immunogenicity. Together, these effects convert immunologically “cold” MSS tumors into an immune-responsive state. Collectively, our findings position ACB1801 as a clinically relevant metabolic-immunomodulatory agent and provide strong preclinical justification for combining harmine derivatives with anti–PD-1 therapy to overcome resistance in MSS CRC patients.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Hill Grading of Gastroesophageal Flap Valve: Model Development and Correlation Validation Against High-Resolution Esophageal Manometry
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Objective To develop an artificial intelligence (AI) model based on ResNet and Hill classification of gastroesophageal flap valve (GEFV) for endoscopic diagnosis of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reduce the subjectivity of manual grading, and provide decision support for clinical GERD risk stratification and anti-reflux therapy selection. Methods In this single-center retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 7,652 endoscopic images from patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) were split into training, validation, and test sets at a patient-level 7:2:1 ratio. A ResNet-152 model was trained with class-weighted cross-entropy loss. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score. Correlation with mean lower esophageal sphincter (LES) pressure from high-resolution manometry (HRM) was assessed in an independent cohort of 92 patients. Results Inter-observer agreement among expert endoscopists yielded a weighted Kappa of 0.73. The final model achieved an overall test-set accuracy of 85.02%, with per-grade accuracies of 84.76%, 80.95%, 76.19%, and 72.38% for Hill grades I–IV, respectively. items.title: Machine Learning and Logistic Regression Models Incorporating Clinical and CT-Derived Muscle-Fat Parameters for Predicting Geriatric Hip Fracture: A Prospective Study
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Hip fractures cause substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Sarcopenia is a key modifiable risk factor, yet few models integrate CT-derived muscle-fat metrics with clinical data. This study aimed to develop a risk prediction model for elderly hip fractures, compare multiple machine learning algorithms, and convert the optimal model into an interpretable nomogram. This prospective cohort enrolled patients aged ≥ 60 years undergoing hip CT, including fracture cases and controls. Muscle/fat area, mean attenuation, and skeletal muscle index were measured at femoral head, lesser trochanter, and L3. The cohort was split 7:3 into training and validation sets. Eight classifiers were built using Boruta-selected features, with performance assessed by AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The logistic regression (LR) achieved the highest AUC (0.779). Multivariable regression retained eight independent predictors: age, elevated glucose, osteoporosis, fat area1/2, muscle mean2, SMI1, and SMI3. The nomogram incorporating these variables showed good discrimination (training AUC = 0.826; validation AUC = 0.817), favorable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.647 and 0.412, respectively), and clinical net benefit on DCA. LR performed comparably or better than other ML algorithms. The nomogram offers a simple, interpretable tool for individualized hip fracture risk stratification using eight routinely available parameters.

items.title: TBX3 is required for the differentiation of a subset of retinal ganglion and cone photoreceptor cells
items.abstract_or_text: Retinogenesis is a key step driving the formation of the neurons that later coordinate angiogenesis in the retina. Understanding these complex interactions requires dissecting apart its cellular and molecular drivers. To tease apart the molecular links coupling retinogenesis to vascular development, we utilized conditional knockout mouse models to selectively delete the transcription factor T-box 3 (Tbx3) in 1) astrocytes, 2) postnatal retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), or 3) retinal progenitors. We demonstrate that the hypovascular retina phenotype observed upon Tbx3 loss most likely stems from a disruption of early retinogenesis. Embryonic analyses revealed that TBX3 is required during a critical retinogenic window coinciding with ATOH7 activity. While ATOH7+ progenitors are more abundant in Tbx3 mutants, the expression of key RGC and cone precursor factors (including TBX5, RXRgamma, ISL1/2, POU4F2, SHH, LHX4 and OTX2) is severely diminished, halting proper RGC and cone differentiation. Utilizing birthdating experiments and developmental immunostaining, we establish TBX3 as a novel upstream regulator of RGC and cone photoreceptor specification. Because the degeneration of RGCs is the definitive hallmark of diseases like glaucoma, identifying TBX3 as a driver of early RGC formation positions it as a promising new candidate biomarker for early-stage glaucoma diagnosis and potentially therapeutic targeting.

items.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
items.abstract_or_text: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. We applied ecCLIP to 67 endogenously tagged RBPs in HEK293T cells, generating a high-quality transcriptome-scale atlas that recovered known binding preferences and captured post-transcriptional regulons linked to RNA half-life. To test the utility of the atlas, we incorporated ecCLIP into Borzuki, a Borzoi-derived sequence-to-function model trained on complementary RNA degradation, expression, CLIP, and Perturb-seq data. Inclusion of ecCLIP data improved RNA half-life prediction and assessment of 3' UTR variant effects on RNA stability, demonstrating that our atlas helps capture RNA dynamics. To directly model the cis-regulatory grammar underlying these RBP-RNA interactions, we developed Pythia, a structure-aware neural network architecture that incorporates context-free grammar-inspired fixed convolutions to explicitly encode RNA base-pairing features. Pythia predicted RBP binding from sequence and structural context and decomposed predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent components. We tested this decomposition for five RBPs using massively parallel reporter CLIP (MPRC) binding assays in cells, using synthetic RNA libraries containing mutations designed to preserve or disrupt predicted RNA structures across nominated binding sites. We used the same MPRC strategy to confirm allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritized by Pythia. Together, ecCLIP and Pythia provide a resource for structure-aware decoding of RNA-protein interaction grammar and interpretation of post-transcriptional regulatory variation.

items.title: A mathematical model of tumor growth driven by oxygen lactate exosome feedback
items.abstract_or_text: Solid tumors develop within a heterogeneous microenvironment shaped by coupled biochemical and metabolic processes. As a tumor grows, oxygen gradients develop from the periphery towards the core, giving rise to hypoxic regions. Hypoxia induces a metabolic shift from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis, leading to elevated lactate production. Experimental studies further indicate that increased lactate levels enhance the secretion of tumor-derived exosomes carrying proteins, mRNA, and lipids, which in turn promote tumor cell proliferation. Together, these interactions form a feedback loop linking oxygen availability, lactate accumulation, and exosome-mediated signaling. Despite growing experimental evidence for each component, the impact of this coupled oxygen lactate exosome axis on tumor growth dynamics has not yet been systematically explored from a mathematical perspective. It remains unclear how the oxygen lactate exosome axis affects tumor growth - impact of nonlocal effects. In this paper, we develop a mechanistic mathematical model to investigate how this feedback mechanisms affects tumor growth. We first consider an in vitro setting oxygen levels are spatially homogeneous and vary periodically in time between normoxic and hypoxic states, capturing key features of cyclic hypoxia observed in vivo. Numerical simulations reveal that exosome mediated feedback has a pronounced effect on tumor volume under chronic hypoxia. In addition, we observe that the tumor volume decreases as the period of cyclic hypoxia increases. We then extend the model to an in vivo framework by incorporating oxygen diffusion and consumption, allowing spatial heterogeneity to emerge. Simulations reveal that tumor cells in normoxic regions benefit indirectly from enhanced exosome secretion driven by lactate produced in hypoxic regions. Overall, the results show how spatially mediated metabolic signaling can amplify tumor growth and aggressiveness, and illustrate how mathematical modeling can increase understanding of non local feedback mechanisms within the tumor microenvironment.

items.title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract_or_text: BACKGROUND: Federal policy now requires sponsors to submit diversity action plans for clinical trials, yet the modifiable features of trial design associated with enrolled composition remain poorly characterized. English-language proficiency requirements are written into eligibility criteria and recorded as free text in a public registry, making them visible and, in principle, amenable to revision, but their relationship to enrolled composition has been examined only within single disease areas and in small samples of trials. We examined whether these requirements and documented language accommodation were associated with the racial and ethnic composition of enrolled participants. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of interventional trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with at least one US site and posted results, using a registry snapshot retrieved in October 2026. The primary cohort comprised the 44,487 trials with exclusively US sites, of which 21,924 (49.3%) reported baseline race and 17,434 (39.2%) reported baseline ethnicity with counts that reconciled with the posted denominator. Both exposures were classified from free-text eligibility criteria using regular expressions validated against independent physician review of 150 trials. For the English-language requirement classifier, sensitivity was 88.2% and specificity was 99.2%. The outcome was the trial-level proportion of enrolled participants in each category, analyzed using generalized linear models adjusted for intervention class, therapeutic area, sponsor, phase, enrollment, sites, start year, US Census region, and the population composition of the trial's site states. An English-language proficiency requirement appeared in 5,736 trials (12.9%); its prevalence rose from 7.4% of trials starting in 2010 to 26.2% in 2023 (odds ratio [OR] per decade 2.91, P<0.001), whereas documented accommodation, an eligibility statement allowing participation in a language other than English (Spanish in 99.9% of flagged trials), remained rare (788 trials, 1.8%). The requirement was associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93, P=0.001) and Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91, P<0.001), with no evidence of an association for White participants (OR=0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.04, P=0.75). Documented accommodation was associated with a higher proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=3.23, 95% CI 2.82-3.71, P<0.001). Geographic adjustment did not change the statistical significance of the requirement associations and attenuated the accommodation association. The main limitations were the cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference; the restriction of enrollment analyses to trials reporting baseline demographics, which were more recent than those without such reporting; and possible misclassification of automatically classified exposures. CONCLUSIONS: English-language proficiency requirements became more than three times as common between 2010 and 2023 and were associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants. Less common documented language accommodation was associated with a higher enrolled proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants. Because these criteria are investigator-written and publicly recorded, they may be a tractable target for improving enrollment equity, although whether revising them changes who enrolls requires prospective evaluation

items.title: Benchmarking Speech Recognition Models for Medical Consultations in Latin American Spanish: A Comparative Evaluation with Fine-Tuning
items.abstract_or_text: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes rely on speech-to-text (STT) models for transcription. Evaluations of STT models in non-English settings remain scarce. We benchmarked ten STT models on medical consultations from Latin American (LatAm) Spanish and assessed whether fine-tuning improves transcription accuracy. METHODS: Ten videos depicting medical consultations. Human transcriptions were the ground truth. Five closed-source models were evaluated: gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gemini-2.5-pro, Eleven Labs, and Assembly AI; and so were five open-source models: Whisper Large, Whisper Large v3, Whisper Large v3 Turbo, Voxtral Mini 3B, and Canary 1B v2. Whisper Large v3, an open-source model, was fine-tuned. One video was withheld from training. Performance assessed using Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER), BLEU Score, ROUGE-L, BERT Score, and Semantic Similarity on the one withheld video. RESULTS: None of the fine-tuning iterations outperformed the vanilla Whisper Large v3. When evaluated on the held-out test video, the fine-tuned open-source Whisper Large v3 did not outperform any of the top closed-source models; conversely, relative to other open-source models, the fine-tuned Whisper Large v3 had superior performance across all metrics, such as in BLEU score (63% vs. 58% for the second-best model), BERT Score (89% vs. 86%), and semantic similarity (89% vs. 83%). CONCLUSIONS: Whisper Large v3 and its fine-tuned variant are the best open-source STT models for transcribing medical conversations in LatAm Spanish. These findings provide evidence for developing AI medical scribes tailored to Spanish-speaking LatAm.

items.title: High-throughput variant libraries and machine learning enable robust target-site selection for toehold-switch design in Detectrons
items.abstract_or_text: Programmable RNA sensors enable sequence-specific detection of RNA inputs for diagnostics, genetic circuit control, and multiplexed molecular readouts. Although readily programmable, their performance varies substantially with the target site selected within a transcript, making target-site selection a major challenge. Here, we report DeSTAR (Detectron Sensor TARget-site ranker), a machine-learning-assisted target-site ranking model for programmable RNA sensors. To train this model, we generated transcript-wide, single-nucleotide-resolution tiling sensor libraries across six diverse RNA targets, enabling generalization to be tested across transcripts rather than within a single RNA. In leave-one-transcript-out evaluation, DeSTAR's top-ranked sites were enriched for high-performing sensors in held-out transcripts, driven predominantly by interpretable sequence grammar in the sensor stem rather than transcript-specific patterns. Prospectively, on an unseen SARS-CoV-2 transcript, the model's top-ranked sites yielded working sensors roughly five-fold more often than random selection. These results support DeSTAR as a generalizable strategy for target-site selection in RNA sensors across transcripts.
